title: NodeLinkRAT campaign hides commands in public notepad pages, targets South Korean users
date_note: Date of the GBHackers report on Genians research; the first phishing email in the campaign was dated 12 September 2026.
actor: Kimsuky (attributed by Genians Security Center, moderate confidence)
summary: GBHackers reports Genians Security Center research on a phishing campaign posing as an aide to a South Korean National Assembly member. A ZIP held a fake Hangul document shortcut that ran hidden PowerShell and set a scheduled task fetching commands from a public aNotepad page, ending in the NodeLinkRAT remote access tool. Genians attributes it to Kimsuky with moderate confidence.
plain: Phishing emails posing as a lawmaker's aide install a remote-access tool on Windows PCs, taking its orders from a public notepad web page. Researchers link it to North Korea's Kimsuky.
exec: Command channels on legitimate note sites evade domain blocking.
action: Block or alert on .lnk files inside ZIP attachments, hunt for a scheduled task named CommonMaintenanceHost, and review outbound access to public notepad sites.

validation.note: GBHackers report of Genians research; Genians original not read.

review.note: Compared ZIP with .hwp.lnk, hidden PowerShell, aNotepad, CommonMaintenanceHost, Kimsuky moderate confidence by Genians against the GBHackers article; single_source disclosed
